Builds the CM3_TEMP folder path in `[0xde279c]` and deletes its files matching the pattern, in groups of 100. \n `utils_clear_temp_folder(pattern)`: builds the temporary folder in `[0xde279c]` (the `CM3_TEMP` variable via 0x90bc50 + "\", if present, and the text of `[0xad9c64]`, copied with a limit by 0x90cf20) and deletes (`remove` 0x94643a) its files that match the pattern, in groups of 100 names (the search is closed before deleting and redone while the group fills up).

Matches a container item name against a pattern with `*` (`*.` goes to the last dot), case-insensitively; the "{ Empty }" slot never matches. \n `zipdir_match_filename_pattern(pattern, name)`: 1 if the item's name matches the pattern. "{ Empty }" (0xad6ad8, the empty slot of the unpack list) never matches; a name equal to the pattern, or an empty pattern, matches; otherwise letter by letter, case-insensitively (0x90c2f0, only the low byte). `*.` skips the name up to the last dot; `*` followed by anything else only matches if it is the end of the pattern. As in the original, the pattern ending before the name also matches ("abc" matches "abcdef").

Adds up the uncompressed sizes of the items matching the pattern (signed int: negative above 2 GB, as in the original). \n `zget_matching_size(path, pattern)`: the sum of the (uncompressed) sizes of the items whose name matches the pattern (0x933a00). The sum is a signed `int`, as in the original: above 2 GB it goes negative and the space check of `load_game_data` always passes (fixing it is a separate decision, like the save above 2 GB). Out of memory, the error box (zipdir.cpp 849) and 0; a container that does not open or is of an unknown type, 0.

Turns each folder file matching the pattern (FindFirstFile) into a container item: zopen for writing, fread/zwrite in 0x30d40-byte blocks, zclose. \n `zadd_matching_files(path, folder, pattern, a4, kind)`: each file in the folder that `FindFirstFile` finds with the pattern (0x4c0aa0/0x4c0b50, files only, in the system's order) becomes a container item: `zopen` for writing (0x9326e0, creates the container with `a4`/`kind` if it does not exist) + `fread` in blocks of 0x30d40 into the item's read buffer (+0x41705) + `zwrite` (0x932e10) + `zclose` (0x932b00). 1 at the end; 0 if nothing matches. A file that does not open or an item refused: the error box (zipdir.cpp 797 / 805) and 0, without closing the search (as the original).

Turns each container item whose name matches the pattern into a folder file (zopen for reading, zread in 0x30d40-byte blocks, fwrite). \n `zextract_matching_files(path, folder, pattern)`: copies the names of the index's 1000 slots (the empty ones as "{ Empty }") into a list of 0x104 bytes per name (malloc 0x944e46); each name that matches the pattern (0x933a00) and opens (`zopen` reading, a4 0x15, kind 4) becomes a file in the folder ("wb"), in blocks of 0x30d40 read by `zread` (0x932c30) into the item's write buffer (+0x72445). 1 if it extracted any. A file that cannot be created: 0 (closes the item). \n Stack garbage in the original: on the error paths (out of memory for the list, a container that does not open or is of an unknown type) it closes the item from a local variable that was never written; here it starts at 0. Out of memory for the index, the error box (zipdir.cpp 642) writes the name "zipdir" over the answer (the same stack slot) and the list carries on without the names (memory from the allocation).

Reads from the item like fread, clipped at the item end; on type 4 decodes the RLE (a run may span calls). \n `zread(buf, size, count, z)` like `fread`, inside the item opened for reading (otherwise 0): the request (`size × count`, int) is clipped at the end of the item and added to the logical position. Type 3: a direct `fread` of `request / size` items. Type 4: decodes the RLE; a run can span calls (+0x10 of +0x14). Returns `request / size` (signed division, as the original: `size` 0 crashes both).

Writes to the item like fwrite and adds to the size in the index; on type 4 encodes the RLE (runs of up to 0x7f kept across calls). \n `zwrite(buf, size, count, z)` like `fwrite`, in the item opened for writing (otherwise 0): adds `size × count` to the item's size in the index and to the logical position. Type 3: a direct `fwrite` (returns whatever it returns). Type 4: encodes the RLE byte by byte, keeping the run in +0x18/+0x14 between calls; a different byte closes the run (1 with byte <= 0x80 goes out as a literal, otherwise the pair 0x80 + n, byte); at 0x7f the pair goes out and the run restarts. Returns `count`.

Closes a container item: when writing, flushes the buffer, closes the pending RLE run and rewrites header and index at the start; closes the file and frees the item. \n `zclose(&z)`. Writing: flushes the write buffer; if the item has a size, on type 4 it closes the pending run directly in the file (literal or pair, as in zwrite) and rewrites the whole header + index (0x416ec bytes) at the start (`fseek` 0). Reading: clears the read cursors. Closes the FILE, frees the ZFILE and clears the pointer.
